newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip in lack-lustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip in lack-lustre trade.

text.p: Egyptian shares lost their lustre on Wednesday in shallow trading, with the all-share index slipping 5.17 points or 1.4 percent to close at 359.58 points.
The Capital Market Authority said in its daily report turnover was worth a below-par 38.19 million pounds ($11.25 million).

"Prices are too low to sell and investors don't have the confidence to buy. The market will not change unless something happens like a good privatisation, not the recent batch which was not encouraging," said broker Dalia Sultan of EFG Hermes.

The state has promised investors it will put up for sale more firms to accelerate its privatisation programme and in the past two weeks, offered investors stakes in several new firms as well as in partly privatised ones already listed on the bourse.
But Sultan said the market needed to be jolted by the sale of bigger tranches in larger companies. "The firms on offer are not good enough. They should sell those with a large capital."

Blue-chip Commercial International Bank (CIB) was one of the most active shares on Wednesday trading in 4.66 million pounds but the stock closed lower 3 pounds at 70.5. "That's one stock investors are buying because the prices are cheap," Sultan said.
But trading was dispirited in all the market's popular sectors, and particularly in the milling sector which ended lower in average turnover.

The cement stocks were also weaker with the exception of Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA which rose 3.45 pounds to 74 pounds in turnover worth 4.66 million pounds. Amriya Cement saw trade worth 1.57 million but fell 2.79 to 83.11.

PACHIN/Paints and Chemical Industries was also one of the day's trend-buckers, rising 1.0 pounds to 120 in 3.60 million pounds of trade. Brokers said the activity was related to the state's sale of 30 percent of PACHIN through a global depository receipt offering expected to be launched soon.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 503.6 points from 517.58 points on Tuesday and the rarely-traded "closed" firms also slipped to 262.92 points from 264.89 points.
Out of 93 shares traded, 30 rose and 39 fell while 24 ended unchanged.
